name: Jurchen
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Jin Guangping & Jin Qizong. 1980. Nüzhen yuyan wenzi yanjiu [Study of the Jurchen language and script]. Beijing: Wenwu chubanshe.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent 重音/声调/重读 finds nothing; scanned too poor to certify silence.

sources.citation: Joseph, Andrew J. 2018. The historical phonology of Manchu dialects. PhD dissertation, Cornell University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Treats Late Jurchen as a Manchu variety (sec.2.2.4, segmental inventory after Kane 1989); states (pp.60-61) that the Manchu accentual system is too poorly described for comparative reconstruction; no Jurchen stress statement.

sources.citation: Pevnov, A. M. 1997. Chzhurchzhen'skij jazyk. In: Alpatov et al. (eds), Jazyki mira: Mongol'skie jazyki. Tunguso-man'chzhurskie jazyki. Japonskij jazyk. Korejskij jazyk. Moskva: Indrik, 260-267.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Short-format Jazyki mira entry; phonology = 5.1.0 tentative phoneme inventory (possible long vowels, no gemination, synharmonism), 5.1.1 syllable structure, 5.1.2 r~l alternation (book pp.261-262). The word udarenie does not occur anywhere in the entry.

sources.citation: Kane, Daniel A. 1975. The Sino-Jurchen vocabulary of the Bureau of Interpreters. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/138579).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Phonology' (pp.41ff.) reconstructs the segmental system phoneme by phoneme against Manchu from the Chinese transcriptions; zero whole-word occurrences of stress/accent/tone in the thesis.

sources.citation: Kane, Daniel & Miyake, Marc Hideo. 2024. Jurchen. In: A. Vovin, J. A. Alonso de la Fuente & J. Janhunen (eds), The Tungusic Languages (Routledge Language Family Series), 76-102. London & New York: Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: The only modern English sketch (Glottolog grammar sketch); Routledge family-volume chapters carry a phonology section that normally addresses prosody, so it is the likeliest place for an explicit statement (even if 'stress not recoverable' or inferred from Manchu).

sources.citation: Sun Bojun 孙伯君. 2004. Jindai Nüzhenyu 金代女真语 [The Jurchen language of the Jin dynasty]. Shenyang: Liaoning minzu chubanshe.

sources.note: Book-length reconstruction of Jin-era (12th-13th c.) Jurchen phonology from Chinese transcriptions in the Jinshi etc; the most detailed phonological treatment, could discuss accent via transcription-character tones.
